title: Mixed-dimension indexing proxy and client negotiation playbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: We need a minimally disruptive path to change embedding dimensionality for new models while continuing to serve existing indices and reranking endpoints with minimal latency/quality regression. This ticket describes a compatibility layer (indexing proxy + client negotiation), online projection/padding strategies, rollout steps, monitoring, and recovery plans.

Goals: 1) Allow serving mixed-dimension indices (e.g., 1024 and 1536) behind a single rerank API without forcing immediate reindexing. 2) Maintain reranker quality within defined deltas (cosine similarity and MRR targets) for upgraded models. 3) Keep tail latency SLOs for rerank and embedding endpoints (p50 < 30ms, p95 < 150ms for small queries). 4) Provide clear developer migration/SDK guidance and measurable cost implications.

Scope: Compatibility proxy for search/rerank, client-side negotiation API, server-side on-the-fly projection library, benchmark harness, observability dashboards, rollout and deprecation schedule. Not included: full-cold reindex orchestration (will reference existing reindex playbooks).
acceptance_criteria: Compatibility proxy routes queries to appropriate index shard without increasing p95 rerank latency by more than 20% under typical load
Automatic projection layer for lower-dim -> higher-dim using learned linear projector and deterministic padding passes A/B quality gates (MRR drop < 2%)
Client SDK exposes vector_schema_version and accepts runtime-negotiation header; server honors migration policy: allow_mixed=true/false
End-to-end integration tests that simulate mixed-dimension queries and verify top-K ordering stable across 90% of test prompts
Dashboard shows per-candidate schema delta, estimated compute cost delta, and reindex backlog with a per-customer migration plan
implementation_notes: Design a lightweight 'indexing-proxy' component that maintains metadata about index shards grouped by schema_version. Proxy selects shard(s) then applies projection/padding when necessary.

Projection strategy: prefer learned linear mapper (small matrix multiply) from lower_dim->higher_dim; fall back to deterministic padding with reserved sentinel dimensions for clients that cannot be updated.
Cache projected vectors for hot documents using TTL-based LRU to avoid repeated projection cost for popular items.

Reranker integration: implement a transparent wrapper that computes pairwise similarities using projected vectors and preserves scoring calibration; include option to store per-document 'native_dim' for debugging.

Client negotiation: new header 'X-Embed-Schema-Version' and SDK handshake that returns 'X-Embed-Schema-Accepted' and recommended migration window. SDKs should expose helper to re-encode older embeddings when uploading.
Benchmarks: microbench (projection latency), end-to-end rerank under 2 traffic shapes (low QPS / high QPS) and adversarial long-seq inputs. Record CPU/GPU cycles and tokenized size impacts.
Cost modelling: estimate projection CPU cost and additional memory for cached projections; produce per-100k-request cost delta for customers running mixed indices.
Data quality evaluation: use existing eval harness but add 'schema_delta' dimension to track whether a query hit native or projected vectors and compare MRR/NDCG per-bucket.
Fallbacks: if projection service latency exceeds threshold, proxy should route to a 'conservative' reranker variant (lower-cost but slightly lower recall) to preserve SLOs.
Telemetry: emit events 'projection_miss', 'projection_hit', 'projection_error', 'schema_negotiation' with minimal cardinality tags (customer, index, schema_version)
Security: projection matrices are model artifacts; treat them as versioned assets with access controls and audit logs.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 - Canary design and infra (owner: infra-tech-lead): spin up proxy in staging, wire observability, add canary indices with mixed dims
Phase 1 - SDK opt-in (owner: SDK-engineering): release SDK patch that sends X-Embed-Schema-Version header. Default behavior: opt-in=false until rollout verification
Phase 2 - Projection service (owner: ml-infra): deploy learned projector and deterministic padding code path; warm caches with synthetic load
Phase 3 - Internal canary (limited customers): enable allow_mixed=true for few low-risk customers, monitor quality and latency for 7 days
Phase 4 - Gradual ramp: increase customer cohort and autoscale proxy; run nightly reindex recommendations and surface per-customer cost estimates
Phase 5 - Deprecation window: publish migration guides and deprecate old schema after 90 days of universal coverage; provide automated reindex tooling as opt-in
test_plan: Unit tests for projection math with fixed RNG seeds and numeric tolerances
Integration tests: end-to-end rerank with mixed-dim corpora, assert ranking stability metrics
Load tests: synthetic replay at 5x and 20x baseline with mixed-dim distribution to measure p95/p99 impact
Chaos tests: simulate projection service outages to verify proxy fallback path and alerting
Calibration tests: verify calibrator preserves score distributions after projection (minimize score drift)
observability: Dashboard: queries/sec by schema_version, projection hit rate, projection latency distribution, p95 rerank latency by schema mix
Alerts: projection error rate > 0.5% for 5m, p95 latency regression > 30% baseline
Quality monitor: nightly MRR/NDCG run; slack report when bucket drift > threshold
Tracing: end-to-end trace including upstream call, projection steps, and similarity computation for debugging
rollbacks_and_risks: Risk: learned linear projector introduces systematic bias for certain languages/domains — mitigate by A/B gating and holdout test sets
Risk: per-request projection adds CPU pressure under bursty traffic — mitigate with caching and pre-projection for hot docs
Rollback: flip proxy flag to 'require_native=true' which rejects mixed queries and forces clients to use compatible schema or use dedicated migration opt-in
Operational runbook: if error budget blown, throttle new mixed-schema traffic, revert SDK opt-ins, and activate emergency reindex advice for affected customers
